question:
The famous Arabic scholar Al Biruni came into contact with India through______________in the eleventh century A.D.

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Abdullah Shah Ghazi
Mahmud Ghaznavi
Al-Walid I
Muhammad Bin Qasim
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mahmud Ghaznavi

Explanation:
Al Biruni was a renowned Arabic scholar, mathematician, and historian who visited India in the 11th century. He came to India with Mahmud Ghaznavi, a Turkic ruler who conducted multiple invasions of India. Al Biruni extensively studied Indian culture, science, religion, and philosophy and documented his findings in his book 'Kitab-ul-Hind' (Tahqiq-e-Hind). This book is a crucial historical document in Arabic about India.

Extra Facts:
Mahmud Ghaznavi invaded India 17 times between 1001 and 1027 CE, with the destruction of the Somnath Temple (1025 CE) being the most infamous. Al Biruni studied Indian astronomy, mathematics, and medicine, learning Sanskrit to translate Indian texts into Arabic.

question_hi:
प्रसिद्ध अरबी विद्वान अल बरूनी ग्यारहवीं शताब्दी ईस्वी (A.D.) में ________ के साथ भारत आया था।

[SSC CGL 2023]
options_hi: अब्दुल्ला शाह गाजी
महमूद गजनवी
अल-वलीद प्रथम
मुहम्मद बिन कासिम
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है महमूद गजनवी

Explanation:
अल बरूनी एक प्रसिद्ध अरबी विद्वान, गणितज्ञ और इतिहासकार थे, जो 11वीं शताब्दी में भारत आए थे। वह महमूद गजनवी के साथ भारत आए, जो एक तुर्की शासक था और उसने भारत पर कई बार आक्रमण किए। अल बरूनी ने भारतीय संस्कृति, विज्ञान, धर्म और दर्शन का गहन अध्ययन किया और अपनी पुस्तक 'किताब-उल-हिंद' (तहकीक-ए-हिंद) में इसका विस्तृत वर्णन किया। यह पुस्तक भारत के बारे में अरबी भाषा में लिखी गई एक महत्वपूर्ण ऐतिहासिक दस्तावेज है।

Extra Facts:
महमूद गजनवी ने 1001 से 1027 ईस्वी के बीच भारत पर 17 बार आक्रमण किए, जिनमें सोमनाथ मंदिर का विध्वंस (1025 ईस्वी) सबसे प्रसिद्ध है। अल बरूनी ने भारतीय ज्योतिष, गणित और चिकित्सा विज्ञान का अध्ययन किया और संस्कृत सीखकर भारतीय ग्रंथों का अरबी में अनुवाद किया।

question:
Who established Sher-i-Adl, an exclusive market in Delhi for manufactured and exported goods to be sold at prices fixed by administration?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah
Muhammad Bin Tughlaq
Alauddin Khalji
Shershah Suri
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Alauddin Khalji

Explanation:
Alauddin Khalji (1296-1316 CE) established an exclusive market in Delhi called Sher-i-Adl, dedicated to manufactured and exported goods sold at government-fixed prices. He implemented several economic reforms, including the creation of the Diwan-i-Riyasat (Commerce Department) and a strict market control system. His policies stabilized the prices of grains, cloth, and essential commodities, benefiting the common people. Alauddin's centralized price regulation was one of the most effective economic measures in medieval India.

Extra Facts:
Alauddin introduced military reforms, such as a permanent army (Dagh system) and cash payments to soldiers. He reimposed the Jizya tax on non-Muslims and enforced strict revenue policies. His price control mechanism is considered a landmark in medieval Indian administration.

question_hi:
प्रशासन द्वारा निर्धारित कीमतों पर बेचे जाने वाले निर्मित और निर्यात किए गए सामानों के लिए दिल्ली में एक विशेष बाजार शेर-ए-अदल की स्थापना किसने की?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: कुतुबुद्दीन मुबारक शाह
मोहम्मद बिन तुगलक
अलाउद्दीन खिलजी
शेरशाह सूरी
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है अलाउद्दीन खिलजी

Explanation:
अलाउद्दीन खिलजी (1296-1316 ई.) ने दिल्ली में शेर-ए-अदल नामक एक विशेष बाजार की स्थापना की थी। यह बाजार निर्मित और निर्यात किए गए सामानों के लिए समर्पित था, जहाँ सभी वस्तुओं की कीमतें प्रशासन द्वारा निर्धारित की जाती थीं। अलाउद्दीन खिलजी ने अपने शासनकाल में कई आर्थिक सुधार किए, जिनमें दीवान-ए-रियासत (वाणिज्य विभाग) की स्थापना और मंडी नियंत्रण प्रणाली शामिल थी। उसने अनाज, कपड़े और अन्य आवश्यक वस्तुओं की कीमतों को स्थिर रखने के लिए कड़े नियम बनाए, जिससे आम जनता को लाभ हुआ।

Extra Facts:
अलाउद्दीन खिलजी ने सैन्य सुधारों के तहत स्थायी सेना (दाग प्रणाली) की शुरुआत की और सैनिकों को नकद वेतन देने की प्रथा शुरू की। उसने जजिया कर को फिर से लागू किया और गैर-मुस्लिमों पर अतिरिक्त कर लगाया। उसकी मूल्य नियंत्रण नीति मध्यकालीन भारत की सबसे प्रभावी आर्थिक नीतियों में से एक मानी जाती है।

question:
The first Turkish ruler who introduced pure Arabic coins in India was ______.

[RPF SI 2024]
options: Alauddin Khilji
Balban
Iltutmish
Qutubuddin Aibak
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Iltutmish

Explanation:
Iltutmish (1211-1236 CE) was the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate to introduce pure Arabic coins in India. He issued 'Tanka' (silver coin) and 'Jital' (copper coin), which were inscribed in Arabic script and followed Islamic traditions. He strengthened the Delhi Sultanate by establishing a centralized administrative and economic system. Iltutmish ensured the purity of silver coins, boosting trade and economy.

Extra Facts:
Iltutmish organized the Iqta system, where land grants were given to officials and soldiers. He completed the construction of the Qutub Minar, initiated by Qutubuddin Aibak. He was the first Sultan of Delhi to receive recognition from the Caliph of Baghdad.

question_hi:
भारत में शुद्ध अरबी सिक्के चलाने वाला पहला तुर्की शासक _____ था।

[RPF SI 2024]
options_hi: अलाउद्दीन खिलजी
बलबन
इल्तुतमिश
कुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है इल्तुतमिश

Explanation:
इल्तुतमिश (1211-1236 ई.) दिल्ली सल्तनत का पहला शासक था जिसने शुद्ध अरबी सिक्के चलाए। उसने 'टंका' (चाँदी का सिक्का) और 'जीतल' (ताँबे का सिक्का) प्रचलित किए। ये सिक्के अरबी लिपि में थे और इस्लामी परंपरा के अनुसार बनाए गए थे। इल्तुतमिश ने दिल्ली सल्तनत को मजबूत करने के लिए केंद्रीकृत प्रशासनिक और आर्थिक प्रणाली विकसित की। उसने चांदी के सिक्कों की शुद्धता सुनिश्चित की, जिससे व्यापार को बढ़ावा मिला।

Extra Facts:
इल्तुतमिश ने इक्ता प्रणाली को संगठित किया, जिसमें सैनिकों और अधिकारियों को भूमि आवंटित की जाती थी। उसने कुतुब मीनार का निर्माण पूरा कराया, जिसे कुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक ने शुरू किया था। वह दिल्ली सल्तनत का पहला शासक था जिसे खलीफा से मान्यता मिली।

question:
______ organized his trusted nobles into a group of forty known as Turkan-i-Chahalgani.

[SSC CGL 2020]
options: Ala-ud-Din Khilji
Balban
Qutub-Ud-Din Aibak
Iltutmish
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Iltutmish

Explanation:
Iltutmish (1211-1236 CE) was a prominent ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who organized a group of his trusted Turkish nobles known as 'Turkan-i-Chahalgani' (The Forty). This group assisted him in administrative and military affairs, strengthening his authority. Iltutmish used this system to stabilize the Delhi Sultanate. The group remained influential until the reign of Balban, who later disbanded it.

Extra Facts:
Iltutmish introduced silver Tanka and copper Jital as standard coins, laying the foundation of the Sultanate's monetary system. He completed the construction of the Qutub Minar, initiated by Qutubuddin Aibak. Iltutmish is regarded as the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate as he shifted the capital from Lahore to Delhi.

[SSC CGL 2020]
options_hi: अला-उद-दीन खिलजी
बलबन
कुतुब-उद-दीन ऐबक
इल्तुतमिश
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है इल्तुतमिश

Explanation:
इल्तुतमिश (1211-1236 ई.) दिल्ली सल्तनत का एक प्रमुख शासक था, जिसने 'तुर्कान-ए-चलागनी' (40 का समूह) नामक एक समूह का गठन किया। यह समूह उसके विश्वसनीय तुर्की अमीरों से मिलकर बना था, जो प्रशासन और सैन्य मामलों में उसकी सहायता करते थे। इल्तुतमिश ने इस समूह के माध्यम से अपनी सत्ता को मजबूत किया और दिल्ली सल्तनत को स्थिरता प्रदान की। यह व्यवस्था बाद में बलबन के शासनकाल तक प्रभावी रही, हालांकि बलबन ने इसे समाप्त कर दिया।

Extra Facts:
इल्तुतमिश ने चांदी का टंका और तांबे का जीतल नामक सिक्के चलवाए, जो दिल्ली सल्तनत की मौद्रिक व्यवस्था के आधार बने। उसने कुतुब मीनार का निर्माण पूरा करवाया, जिसकी नींव कुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक ने रखी थी। इल्तुतमिश को दिल्ली सल्तनत का वास्तविक संस्थापक माना जाता है, क्योंकि उसने ही राजधानी को लाहौर से दिल्ली स्थानांतरित किया।

question:
Which of the following Sultans of Delhi primarily adopted a policy of consolidation rather than expansion?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Ibrahim Lodi
Balban
Alauddin Khalji
Bahlol Lodi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Balban

Explanation:
Ghiyasuddin Balban (1266-1286 CE) was a prominent Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate who primarily adopted a policy of consolidation rather than expansion. His reign is known for internal security and administrative reforms. Balban enforced the 'Iron and Blood' policy to suppress rebels and dissenters. He established the Spah-i-Bidawat (spy network) to prevent rebellions. He defended the Sultanate from Mongol invasions and strengthened military power. Balban promoted the Divine Right Theory of Kingship (Naseer-e-Ilahi), elevating the Sultan's status to a divine level.

Extra Facts:
Balban reduced the influence of the Chalisa (group of 40 nobles). He crushed the rebellion of Tughril Khan in Bengal. His reign strengthened the military and administrative system of the Delhi Sultanate, laying a strong foundation for future rulers.

question_hi:
दिल्ली के निम्नलिखित में से किस सुल्तान ने मुख्य रूप से विस्तार के बजाय सुदृढ़ीकरण की नीति अपनाई?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options_hi: इब्राहीम लोदी
बलबन
अलाउद्दीन खिलजी
बहलोल लोदी
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है बलबन

Explanation:
गयासुद्दीन बलबन (1266-1286 ईस्वी) दिल्ली सल्तनत का एक प्रमुख सुल्तान था जिसने मुख्य रूप से साम्राज्य के सुदृढ़ीकरण की नीति अपनाई। उसका शासनकाल आंतरिक सुरक्षा और प्रशासनिक सुधारों के लिए जाना जाता है। बलबन ने 'लौह एवं रक्त' की नीति अपनाकर विद्रोहियों और असंतुष्टों को कठोरता से दबाया। उसने स्पाह-ए-बिदौत (जासूस नेटवर्क) की स्थापना की ताकि विद्रोहों को रोका जा सके। उसने मंगोल आक्रमणों से सल्तनत की रक्षा की और सैन्य शक्ति को मजबूत किया। बलबन ने राजत्व के सिद्धांत (नसीर-ए-इलाही) को बढ़ावा दिया, जिससे सुल्तान की स्थिति दैवीय हो गई।

Extra Facts:
बलबन ने चालीसा (40 अमीरों के समूह) के प्रभाव को कम करने का प्रयास किया। उसने बंगाल में तुगरिल खान के विद्रोह को कुचल दिया। बलबन के शासनकाल में दिल्ली सल्तनत की सैन्य और प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था मजबूत हुई, जिसने भविष्य के शासकों के लिए एक मजबूत आधार तैयार किया।

question:
Who among the following Sultans framed a series of regulations to weaken the power of nobles?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Muhammad bin Tughluq
Balban
Alauddin Khilji
Iltutmish
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Alauddin Khilji

Explanation:
Alauddin Khilji (1296-1316 CE) implemented a series of strict regulations to weaken the power of the nobles (amirs) during his reign. He introduced the 'Market Control System', where soldiers and officials were paid in cash to reduce their dependence on nobles. He restricted the jagirdari system and directly collected land revenue. Additionally, he banned alcohol and lavish parties to diminish the social influence of the nobles. These reforms were part of his 'centralized governance' aimed at strengthening the Sultan's authority.

Extra Facts:
Alauddin Khilji strengthened the Delhi Sultanate as a military power. He fortified border security to prevent Mongol invasions and conquered Devagiri (Deccan). His price control policy (Dagh and Chehra) controlled inflation, which was revolutionary for that era.

question:
Quwwat-al-islam mosque is nearest to which of the following historical monuments ?

[RPF SI 2024]
options: Tughlakabad Fort
Qutub Minar
Jama Masjid
Humayun Tomb
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Qutub Minar

Explanation:
The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque is an ancient mosque located in Delhi, built by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1193 CE. It is one of the earliest significant Islamic structures in India. This mosque is situated within the Qutub Minar complex, constructed during the Delhi Sultanate period. The Qutub Minar stands adjacent to the mosque, and both are part of the same historical complex. Hence, the nearest historical monument to the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque is the Qutub Minar.

Extra Facts:
The Qutub Minar is a 73-meter-high tower, initiated by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by Iltutmish. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a masterpiece of Indo-Islamic architecture. The complex also houses the Iron Pillar, which has remained rust-free for nearly 1600 years.

question:
Balban served as naib to which of the following sultans of Delhi?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Iltutmish
Razia
Nasiruddin Mahmud
Qutb ud-Din Aibak
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nasiruddin Mahmud

Explanation:
Balban served as the naib (deputy) to Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-1266 CE) of the Delhi Sultanate. A powerful and ambitious Turkish slave, Balban took advantage of the Sultan's weakness and consolidated real power in his own hands. He adopted the title 'Ulugh Khan' and introduced administrative and military reforms. Balban followed the 'Blood and Iron' policy, crushing rebellions by Rajputs and Mongol invasions. After Nasiruddin's death, Balban himself ascended the throne in 1266 CE.

Extra Facts:
Balban promoted the Persian theory of kingship, calling himself 'Zill-e-Ilahi' (Shadow of God). He introduced the celebration of 'Nowruz' (Persian New Year) as a royal festival. He established the 'Diwan-i-Arz' (Military Department) and abolished the 'Chalisa' (Group of Forty Turkish nobles).

question:

Explanation:
Ibn Batuta, a famous Moroccan traveller, visited India in the 14th century. In his travelogue 'Rihla', he mentioned that the people of Delhi used to write abusive letters to Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Angered by this, the Sultan decided to shift the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad as a form of punishment. This decision was one of the controversial policies of the Sultan, earning him the nickname 'Mad Sultan'.

Extra Facts:
Ibn Batuta extensively documented the rule of the Tughlaq dynasty during his travels. According to him, Muhammad bin Tughlaq implemented several unconventional policies, such as introducing copper currency and forcibly relocating Delhi's entire population to Daulatabad. These policies proved highly controversial and ultimately weakened his reign.

इब्न बतूता ने अपनी यात्रा में भारत के अलावा अफ्रीका, मध्य एशिया, चीन और दक्षिण-पूर्व एशिया के कई देशों का भी भ्रमण किया। उसका यात्रा वृत्तांत मध्यकालीन भारत के इतिहास का एक महत्वपूर्ण स्रोत है। मोहम्मद बिन तुगलक के शासनकाल को दिल्ली सल्तनत के विस्तार और विवादों के लिए जाना जाता है। उसने दौलताबाद को राजधानी बनाने का प्रयास किया, जो असफल रहा।

Who among the following is the author of the book 'Tabaqat-i-Nasiri'?

It serves as a crucial source for understanding medieval Indian history.

Extra Facts:
Minhaj-us-Siraj documented the expansion of Islamic rule in India, the policies of the Slave Dynasty rulers, and the impact of the Mongol invasions. Written in Persian, this text is considered a key reference for studying the political and social history of medieval India.

question:
How many dynasties ruled Delhi during the Sultanate period (1206 AD – 1526 AD)?

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options: 6
4
5
3
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 5

Explanation:
During the Delhi Sultanate period (1206 AD – 1526 AD), a total of 5 dynasties ruled Delhi. These are - Slave Dynasty (1206-1290), Khilji Dynasty (1290-1320), Tughlaq Dynasty (1320-1414), Sayyid Dynasty (1414-1451), and Lodi Dynasty (1451-1526). These dynasties played a crucial role in Indian history, including administrative reforms, cultural development, and military expansion. This period saw the establishment of a centralized governance system in North India.

Extra Facts:
The Slave Dynasty was founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, while Iltutmish strengthened it. Alauddin Khilji introduced market controls and military reforms. Muhammad bin Tughlaq made the controversial decision to shift the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad. The last ruler of the Lodi Dynasty, Ibrahim Lodi, was defeated by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat (1526), marking the beginning of the Mughal Empire.

question:
Delhi Sultanate signifies the rule over India with capital as Delhi, of which community ?

[RPF SI 2024]
options: Arabian
African
Turkish
Persian
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Turkish

Explanation:
The Delhi Sultanate (1206-1526 CE) was a Muslim empire ruling over India, founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak. It was primarily ruled by rulers of Turkish origin, who established Islamic rule in India. The Sultanate is divided into five dynasties - Slave Dynasty, Khilji Dynasty, Tughlaq Dynasty, Sayyid Dynasty, and Lodi Dynasty. Most rulers were of Turkic or Turko-Afghan descent. This period saw the development of the Iqta system, new coinage, and architecture (e.g., Qutub Minar).

Extra Facts:
During the Delhi Sultanate, Persian language dominated as the administrative and cultural language. Balban (1266-1286) adopted the 'Blood and Iron' policy, while Alauddin Khilji (1296-1316) implemented market controls and military reforms. Muhammad bin Tughlaq's (1325-1351) controversial decisions (capital shift, token currency) weakened the Sultanate.

question:
Who among the following built the Alai Darwaza in Delhi in 1311?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Allauddin Khilji
Muhammad-bin-Tughluq
Iltutmish
Firoz Shah Tughlaq
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Allauddin Khilji

Explanation:
Allauddin Khilji (1296-1316 CE) built the Alai Darwaza in Delhi in 1311. It is located in the Qutub Minar complex and is a masterpiece of Indo-Islamic architecture . Made of red sandstone , it features intricate geometric and floral carvings . The gate symbolized the power and prosperity of the Khilji dynasty. Allauddin constructed it as part of his expansion plan for the Qutub Minar complex.

Extra Facts:
The Alai Darwaza is considered the first pure Islamic structure in India, as it lacks Hindu architectural elements. Allauddin also built the Siri Fort and Hazar Sutun (Palace of a Thousand Pillars). He implemented a price control system to stabilize market rates.

question:
Which of the following events took place in 1398?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: Timur invasion of india
Battle of Haldighati
Babur's invasion of Delhi
Humayun's flight to Persia
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Timur invasion of India

Explanation:
In 1398, Timur (Tamerlane) invaded India, marking a significant event in medieval Indian history. Timur attacked during the reign of the Tughlaq dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate and looted Delhi. His invasion symbolized political chaos and weakness in India. Timur massacred thousands and carried out extensive plundering, severely weakening the Delhi Sultanate. This event was one of the precursors to the establishment of the Mughal Empire in India.

Extra Facts:
Timur was a powerful Central Asian ruler who established a vast empire. His invasion of India was primarily motivated by the desire for wealth. He defeated the then Sultan of Delhi, Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughlaq. After Timur's invasion, the Delhi Sultanate became extremely weak, paving the way for Babur to invade India later.

question:
Who among the following constructed the garrison town Siri for his soldiers?

[RRB NTPC CBT]

Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq

Mohammad Tughluq
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Alauddin Khilji

Explanation:
Alauddin Khilji (1296-1316 CE) constructed the garrison town of Siri for his soldiers. It was one of the first planned military towns of the Delhi Sultanate. Alauddin built Siri to defend against Mongol invasions and to organize his army efficiently. He also implemented administrative systems like 'Naya Bazaar' (New Market) and 'Diwan-i-Riyasat' to provide goods to soldiers at controlled prices. The construction of Siri was a key part of his military and economic policies.

Extra Facts:
Alauddin Khilji introduced the Market Control System, fixing prices of grains, cloth, and essential commodities. He strictly enforced the Jizya tax and initiated military reforms like the Dagh system (Huliya method), where horses were branded for identification.

question:
'Adhai-Din-Ka-Jhonpra' is one of the oldest mosques situated in ______.

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options: Hyderabad
Ajmer
Cuttack
Burhanpur
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ajmer

Explanation:
'Adhai-Din-Ka-Jhonpra' is located in Ajmer, Rajasthan, and is one of the oldest mosques in India. It was built in 1192 CE under the orders of Muhammad Ghori. Originally, it was a Sanskrit college, later converted into a mosque. The name 'Adhai-Din-Ka-Jhonpra' (meaning 'Hut of Two-and-a-Half Days') comes from the belief that it was constructed in just two-and-a-half days. It is an excellent example of Indo-Islamic architecture, featuring intricately carved pillars similar to those in the Qutub Minar.

Extra Facts:
Ajmer was a significant city in medieval India and is also famous for the Dargah of Sufi saint Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti. Qutub-ud-din Aibak supervised the construction of this mosque. The site reflects the early Delhi Sultanate architecture.

गयासुद्दीन बलबन (1266-1286 ई.) ने दिल्ली सल्तनत के दौरान मेवाती समुदाय से निपटने के लिए 'रक्त और लौह' (blood and iron) की नीति अपनाई थी। मेवाती लोग अक्सर दिल्ली के आसपास के क्षेत्रों में लूटपाट करते थे और सल्तनत के लिए एक बड़ी चुनौती थे। बलबन ने कठोर दमन नीति अपनाई, जिसमें उसने मेवातियों के गढ़ों को नष्ट कर दिया और उनके नेताओं को क्रूरता से दंडित किया। उसने अपनी सेना को मजबूत करके और सैन्य शक्ति के प्रदर्शन द्वारा विद्रोहियों को डराने की कोशिश की। बलबन का यह दृष्टिकोण उसकी 'लौह और रक्त' नीति का हिस्सा था, जिसका उद्देश्य सल्तनत में कानून और व्यवस्था बहाल करना था।

Extra Facts:
बलबन ने सल्तनत को मजबूत करने के लिए कई अन्य सुधार भी किए, जैसे 'सिजदा' (झुककर प्रणाम) और 'पैबोस' (पैर चूमना) जैसी प्रथाएं शुरू कीं ताकि सुल्तान की प्रतिष्ठा बढ़े। उसने तुर्कान-ए-चिहालगानी (40 तुर्क अमीरों का समूह) के प्रभाव को कम करके केंद्रीकृत शासन स्थापित किया। उसने मंगोल आक्रमणों से बचाव के लिए सीमा क्षेत्रों को मजबूत किया।

question:
During the Sultanate of Delhi, the term "Ulema" was associated with ______.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Learned theologians and Jurists
Commander-in-chief
Postal officer
Village Revenue officer
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Learned theologians and Jurists

Explanation:
During the Delhi Sultanate, the term 'Ulema' referred to Islamic scholars and jurists who were experts in Islamic law (Sharia). They advised the Sultan on religious and legal matters and played a crucial role in shaping the policies of the Sultanate. The Ulema included Qazis (judges), Muftis (jurists), and Imams, who held significant influence in society due to their religious authority.

Extra Facts:
The Ulema were instrumental in administering education and justice during the Delhi Sultanate. They managed madrasas (Islamic schools) and promoted Islamic teachings. Sultans like Iltutmish and Balban sought the support of the Ulema to legitimize their rule through religious policies.

Explanation:

question:
Quwwat al-Islam mosque and minaret, built during the last decade of the ______ century.

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Eleventh
Thirteenth
Fourteenth
Twelfth
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Twelfth

Explanation:
The Quwwat al-Islam Mosque and its famous Qutub Minar were constructed in the last decade of the 12th century (1192-1198 CE) by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. This mosque is one of the earliest in India and was built using remnants of Hindu and Jain temples. The Qutub Minar was later expanded by Iltutmish and Alauddin Khalji. It is a masterpiece of Indo-Islamic architecture.

Extra Facts:
The Qutub Minar is the world's tallest brick minaret (73 meters). Red sandstone and marble were used in its construction. The name Quwwat al-Islam translates to "Might of Islam" in Arabic. This site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

[SSC CGL 2022]

तेरहवीं
चौदहवीं
बारहवीं
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है बारहवीं

Explanation:
कुव्वत अल-इस्लाम मस्जिद और उसकी प्रसिद्ध कुतुब मीनार का निर्माण 12वीं सदी के अंतिम दशक (1192-1198 ई.) में हुआ था। यह दिल्ली सल्तनत के पहले शासक कुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक द्वारा बनवाई गई थी। यह मस्जिद भारत की पहली मस्जिदों में से एक है और इसका निर्माण हिंदू व जैन मंदिरों के अवशेषों से किया गया था। कुतुब मीनार को बाद में इल्तुतमिश और अलाउद्दीन खिलजी ने और ऊँचा बनवाया। यह इंडो-इस्लामिक वास्तुकला का एक उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है।

Extra Facts:
कुतुब मीनार विश्व की सबसे ऊँची ईंटों से बनी मीनार है (73 मीटर)। इसके निर्माण में लाल बलुआ पत्थर और संगमरमर का उपयोग हुआ। कुव्वत अल-इस्लाम मस्जिद का नाम अरबी में "इस्लाम की ताकत" के रूप में अनुवादित होता है। यह स्थल यूनेस्को की विश्व धरोहर सूची में शामिल है।
